clue.text: See 23
Name for the new arrival?

parts.note: a baby or anything else freshly arrived has 'just' come 'in', and run together those two words make a boy's first name

explanation.surface: Parents wondering what to call their newborn baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the boy's name reads as a phrase meaning newly arrived, so it suits a newborn.

clue.text: London district with no healthy bank

indicators.note: with no tells us to take the second word's synonym away from the district's name

parts.note: Camberwell is a district of south London
healthy means well

explanation.surface: A part of London whose bank is in poor financial health.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMBERWELL is an area of south London; 'bank' looks like a lender but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the sloping bank or tilt built into a road surface or track.

clue.text: Set of data held by second team about member of same club?

indicators.note: held by means the data set sits inside the letters around it
about signals that the letters of team are turned around into a new order

parts.note: a table is a set of data laid out in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A data table kept by a reserve side, describing a fellow club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team' looks like part of the club setting, but it is only letters to rearrange; 'held by' sets the data inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse from the same racing stable, or by extension a colleague from the same organisation.

clue.text: Scents of flowers newly opened

indicators.note: newly gives N for new, and opened says it replaces the first letter of the flowers

parts.note: roses are flowers

explanation.surface: The perfume of blooms that have just come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' stands for N (new), which takes over the opening letter of ROSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose is the smell or bouquet of a wine, so the plural means scents.

clue.text: Old-fashioned dance, half-forgotten by one found in crashed car

indicators.note: found in means the dance and the one go inside the wrecked car letters
crashed says the letters of car are smashed into a new order
half-forgotten means half of the dance's name is dropped

parts.note: the cha-cha is a Latin dance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old dance routine, partly forgotten by someone pulled from a car wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-forgotten' keeps one half of the doubled dance name; 'crashed' scrambles the car, which 'found in' wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something belonging to an earlier era and now outdated.

clue.text: Bulk in diet adjusted with addition of a plum duff

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters of the diet, joined by the plum, are rearranged
duff, meaning faulty, is a second hint that these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A diet changed by adding a plum pudding, which would bulk anyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum duff is a British steamed pudding, so 'duff' looks like part of the food; it means 'no good', a second anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplitude means largeness or breadth, so it can stand for bulk or size.

clue.text: Somewhat nicer term for a banker

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gentler word for someone who works in finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests a city financier, but in betting a banker is a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing slang a cert is a certainty, as is a banker, a bet that cannot lose.

clue.text: Perfumed woman stripped on board lorry

indicators.note: on board means being carried inside the vehicle's letters

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters of woman are removed

explanation.surface: A scented woman undressing on the back of a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' strips W and N off WOMAN, leaving OMA; ARTIC is British slang for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means fragrant, having a pleasant strong smell, as something perfumed does.

clue.text: Irish girls against eating fish left over on Saturday?

indicators.note: eating means the reversed piece goes inside the word for against

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: over says the fish and left together are turned round

parts.note: an eel is a fish
S is short for Saturday

explanation.surface: Irish girls who object to eating leftover fish at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left over' looks like leftovers, but 'left' gives a letter and 'over' turns it and the fish round; 'eating' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleen is an Irish word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Man or woman with a degree in Dance

parts.note: Sam can be short for Samuel or Samantha, so it suits either sex
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone of either sex holding a degree in dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance.

clue.text: Big game bird that's magnificent?

parts.note: superb means magnificent
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A hunting question: is a splendid bird big game?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' suggests hunting trophies, but it is the American football championship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the NFL's annual championship match, the biggest game of the US season.

clue.text: Quote girl's reflection about boxer shorts: "Ultimately impractical"

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go round the boxer and the last letter
reflection, as in a mirror, means the quote and the girl are read backwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite
Di is a girl's name
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer

indicators.note: Ultimately picks the final letter of the word shorts

explanation.surface: A girl's thoughts on boxer shorts, quoted as being impractical in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer shorts' looks like underwear; 'Ultimately' looks part of the definition but picks the last letter of 'shorts'. 'reflection' reads quote and girl backwards; 'about' wraps them round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealistic plan aims at perfection rather than what can be done, so it is unrealistic.

clue.text: Variety of red wine, say, in an excessive amount

definitions.meaning: a crimson pigment, a shade of red

definitions.text: wine, say, in an excessive amount
definitions.meaning: a wine ... is a huge surplus of wine, as stored up under EU farm policy

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a reddish pigment and also, as in milk or wine lake, a large surplus.

clue.text: Coward from York originally, caught in Tadcaster dancing topless

indicators.note: in means the two letters are put inside the scrambled town
dancing says the remaining letters of the town move into a new order
topless means the town's first letter is removed
originally picks the first letter of York

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A coward from York caught dancing topless in a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tadcaster is a Yorkshire town. 'topless' drops its T, 'dancing' makes SCAREDAT from ADCASTER, and Y and C go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaredy-cat is a childish name for a timid person or coward.

clue.text: See 17
Fortunate quality, having courage when powerless

indicators.note: when powerless means the abbreviation for power is taken out

parts.note: pluckiness means courage

explanation.surface: Being lucky means having courage when you lack power.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the usual abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: Luckiness is the state of being lucky or fortunate, a quality someone has.

clue.text: Game with policeman specially assigned to unruly crowd

parts.note: SC stands for special constable, a volunteer police officer
a rabble is an unruly crowd

explanation.surface: A game in which a special officer is sent to control a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the board game in which players build words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Boob getting bared, with row ensuing?

definitions.text: Boob getting bared, with row ensuing?

indicators.note: ensuing means the boob comes after, following the first word
getting, read as becoming something else, lets the bared and row letters turn into a new word

parts.note: a boob is a blunder or failure, a thing gone wrong

explanation.surface: A garment slips and exposes a breast, and a scandal follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's idea runs in reverse: the first word, made to 'malfunction', gives 'bared' and 'row'. Read forwards, the two words rearranged give the first word, and 'Boob' (a blunder) gives the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a blunder, and a wardrobe malfunction is a clothing blunder.

clue.text: Cock starts to crow heartily as night turns into coming light, East End rising

indicators.note: starts to means we take the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.words: crow heartily as night turns into coming light, East End rising

explanation.surface: A rooster crows loudly as night gives way to dawn rising in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the rooster of medieval fable, as in Chaucer; 'East End' suggests London but just gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is a traditional literary name for a rooster.

clue.text: Row about doctor's warning call

indicators.note: about means the row goes around the doctor

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: An argument over a doctor's warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks shout this word to warn that a felled tree is about to fall.

clue.text: Harmonised with a good clarinet part?

parts.note: a clarinet's mouthpiece holds a reed

explanation.surface: Was the music in harmony with a good clarinet section?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmonised' suggests music, but here it means came to agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to be in harmony or accord, so agreed means harmonised.

clue.text: Assistant thought last must be first

indicators.note: last must be first means the final letter moves to the front

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A helper who believes the last shall be first.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: Making wrong call, "Muggins" DJ is cut off

indicators.note: off says the letters are out of place and must be reordered
cut means the word is is docked of its last letter

explanation.surface: A fool of a disc jockey gets taken off the air for a bad decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks IS to I and 'off' scrambles MUGGINSDJI. Muggins is British slang for a fool, usually oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Misjudging is getting an assessment or decision wrong, as a referee making a bad call does.

clue.text: Catch sailor in the bosom of mythical Greek singer

indicators.note: in the bosom of means placed in the middle of the Greek hero's name

parts.note: Jason led the Argonauts in Greek myth
to net is to catch
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Trapping a seaman in the chest of a legendary Greek singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bosom' nods to the pop star's 2004 Super Bowl incident in the linked clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet Jackson is an American pop singer, sister of Michael.

clue.text: Regularly find clues not working

indicators.note: Regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps finding clues while doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive, so a machine or person not in use is not working.

clue.text: Plant health food around hole next to a prepared bed

indicators.note: around means the health food is wrapped about the other pieces

parts.note: bran is a high-fibre health food
O is a hole by its shape

indicators.note: prepared says the letters of bed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant set in a hole by a prepared bed, with healthy food around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'health food' is one piece, not part of the plant; 'prepared' scrambles bed and 'around' wraps the food about the hole, the A and the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad bean is a plant grown for its large flat edible seeds.

clue.text: Organisation giving advice on the overseas TV network?

parts.note: CAB is the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British charity giving free advice
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: An advice bureau's view of a foreign television network.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: cable is a TV delivery network.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable television delivers channels to homes through a network of wires.

clue.text: Small holes in steel forged after turning the 5 across

indicators.note: after puts the forged metal behind the turned word
turning means the old form of the word is read backwards

parts.note: ye is the old-fashioned form of the, and 5 across asks for an old-fashioned word

indicators.note: forged means the steel is beaten into a new shape, so its letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Small holes punched into steel that has been forged.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5 across' answer is ARCHAIC, so 'the 5 across' is YE; 'turning' gives EY and 'forged' turns STEEL into ELETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelets are small reinforced holes, as for laces in shoes.

clue.text: To read article out in French you first must be taught

indicators.note: first places the French pronoun before the rest

parts.note: tu is the French for you

indicators.note: out means the article is removed from the words before it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Before you can read, you must be taught in French first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tutored is to be taught, especially privately by a tutor.
